text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on April 11 in history:
1514 - Donato Bramante, Italian architect, died; the last 15 years of his life were spent working for Popes Alexander VI and Julius II.
1689 - William III of Orange and Mary II were crowned joint monarchs of Great Britain.
1713 - The Treaty of Utrecht was signed, ending the War of the Spanish Succession and re-drawing the map of Europe. Signatories included Spain, Britain, France, Holland, Portugal and Prussia.
1755 - James Parkinson, British physician who discovered Parkinson's disease, born.
1805 - The Treaty of St Petersburg was signed under which Russia and Britain agreed to form an alliance, the Third Coalition, against France.
1814 - Under the Treaty of Fontainebleau, Napoleon abdicated and was banished to the Isle of Elba; Louis XVIII acceeded to the throne.
1819 - Sir Charles Halle, German pianist and conductor, born. He settled in Manchester after being driven to England by the 1848 Revolution and in 1858 founded the famous Halle Orchestra.
1884 - Charles Reade, English novelist, notably "The Cloister and the Hearth", died.
1893 - U.S. politician and Secretary of State from 1949-1953, Dean Acheson, born. He helped to formulate the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan and promoted the setting up of NATO.
1894 - Uganda was declared a British protectorate.
1906 - James Anthony Bailey, U.S. circus owner, and half of the Barnum and Bailey partnership, died.
1913 - French pilot Gustave Hamel made a record return trip across the Channel from Dunkirk to Dover and back in only 90 minutes.
1919 - The constitution of the International Labour Organisation came into effect.
1926 - Luther Burbank, American botanist and plant breeder, died. He developed the Burbank potato as well as new fruits and flowers.
1945 - American troops captured the German towns of Essen and Weimar and liberated the Buchenwald concentration camp.
1951 - President Truman dismissed General Douglas MacArthur from all his posts including that of United Nations Forces Commander in Korea for making critical political statements.
1951 - The Stone of Scone was recovered after an 107 day hunt after it had been stolen from Westminster Abbey by Scottish Nationalists who wanted it returned to Scotland.
1952 - The Movimiento Nacionalista Revolucionario (MNR) seized power in Bolivia in a bloody coup.
1957 - Singapore was granted self-government by the United Kingdom.
1961 - Former SS Officer Adolf Eichmann's trial began in Jerusalem for his part in war crimes against Jews during World War Two.
1970 - The U.S. spacecraft Apollo 13 was launched on its ill-fated journey to the moon. Forced to turn back due to an on-board explosion, it landed safely on the 17th.
1979 - The Ugandan capital Kampala fell to a combined force of Ugandan exiles and Tanzanian troops, ending the eight-year rule of Idi Amin who fled to Libya.
1982 - British explorer Ranulph Fiennes with Charles Burton became the first explorers to complete a circumnavigation of the Earth via the Poles when they reached the North Pole.
1984 - Konstantin Chernenko was appointed President of the Soviet Union.
1990 - British customs officers seized barrels or piping bound for Iraq believed to be part of a "supergun'.
1994 - Communists and their allies outpolled nationalist rivals in Ukraine's first post-Soviet general election, filling nearly a quarter of the seats.
1996 - Forty-three African states signed a treaty declaring Africa free of nuclear weapons at a ceremony marred by Russian reservations about the document.
1996 - Fire swept through Germany's second biggest airport at Duesseldorf, killing 16 people.
